\section{Projection certificate and Gaussian law}
\label{app:gaussian}

Let $E_\ell:\R^6\to C^2(K;\R)$ insert the six oriented coordinate vectors
of a star before the orientation signs are applied.  The certificate exhibits
a rational matrix $X_\ell\in\mathbb Q^{216\times6}$ and sets
$Y_\ell=d_1X_\ell$.  It verifies exactly that
\[
 d_1^\mathsf T(E_\ell-Y_\ell)=0.
\]
Thus $Y_\ell\in\im d_1$ and $E_\ell-Y_\ell\perp\im d_1$, proving
$Y_\ell=PE_\ell$ without trusting a numerical pseudoinverse.

For a canonical interior link, the resulting oriented centered covariance is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:exact-K}
 K_\ell=\frac1{3780}
 \begin{pmatrix}
1369&-239&-239&-413&-239&-239\\
-239&1369&-239&-239&-413&-239\\
-239&-239&1369&-239&-239&-413\\
-413&-239&-239&1369&-239&-239\\
-239&-413&-239&-239&1369&-239\\
-239&-239&-413&-239&-239&1369
 \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
The three opposite-pair antisymmetric vectors have eigenvalue
$1782/3780=33/70$.  On the opposite-pair symmetric subspace, the reduced
matrix has diagonal $956/3780$ and off-diagonal $-478/3780$; hence its all-one
mode has eigenvalue zero and its two sum-zero modes have eigenvalue
$1434/3780=239/630$.  This proves the displayed spectrum.

If $F$ has covariance $tP\otimes I_3$, an orthogonal scalar eigenbasis makes
the five nonzero modes independent, each with three color components.  This
gives the weighted $\chi^2_3$ representation.  For $s<35/(33t)$,
\begin{align*}
 \E e^{sQ_\ell}
 &=\left(1-\frac{239}{315}st\right)^{-3}
   \left(1-\frac{33}{35}st\right)^{-9/2}.
\end{align*}
Markov's inequality and optimization over $s$ yield the stated Chernoff rate.

The exact normal equations and characteristic polynomial are checked for all
eight interior links, not inferred from the apparent equality of floating
spectra.
